recommendation: I'd write post 3, the ATS score panel, next — it's the natural follow-up to your tracker post and keeps your Build in Public arc moving while your audience is already invested in the JobMatch story. Frame it around the visual breakdown of how a CV matches a job description, since that's a tangible, screenshot-able feature people can immediately see the value of. Bonus: it ties straight back to your fit-score origin story, so it reinforces the through-line of the whole project.

draft.text:
When I started JobMatch, the whole thing was one number.

You paste a job description, and the app gives you a fit score out of 10 with reasoning. That was phase one, and honestly it was enough to make me feel less lost during my own search.

But a single number always bothered me. A 6 out of 10 tells you something is off. It doesn't tell you what.

So the feature I'm building now is an ATS score panel. Instead of just a number, it breaks down exactly how my CV lines up against the job description. Which keywords landed, which ones are missing, where the gaps are.

It turns a vague feeling into something I can actually fix before I hit apply.

What I like is how it closes a loop. The project started with a fit score, and now I'm building the panel that explains that score. Same idea, just honest enough to show its work.

Coming from hospitality, this is the part that feels familiar. You don't get to guess whether a guest had a good stay. You look at the details and you adjust.

I'm still surprised that the thing I built to help me find a job is the thing teaching me the most about building.
